svg.title: Spectral fragment index: original and compact byte layouts
svg.desc: Byte-accurate diagrams of 16 and 32 bit local precursor records, original and compact fragment-mass bins, the rank mask, Float32 bounds, unchanged RT bins, and decoding into native RAM arrays. Byte counts exclude serialization headers and compression.

g.text: Original native layout → compact disk encoding → identical native layout in RAM
Array payloads before Zlib compression · offsets are zero-based · integer byte order shown: little-endian
Each numbered cell is one byte. All bits in the ID and rank mask are data; hatched cells are alignment padding.
COMPACT · IDs and masks stored in separate arrays
2 B + 1 B = 3 B per entry · 25% less payload
4 B + 1 B = 5 B per entry · 37.5% less payload
IDs are unsigned integers with no embedded flags. Masks retain all eight bits in both formats.
Each row below is one element of a separate array—not one contiguous struct. Byte-cell width is the same on both sides.
Exact integer addition on Float32 bit patterns; no m/z rounding.
Only the end offset is stored for each contiguous entry range.
One delta width is chosen for the entire partition:
SIMD tail: seven Float32 +∞ values (28 B) are replaced by a padding count and recreated on load.
Field widths stay exact; the compact file changes their arrangement and removes derivable fields.
One bit per selected index rank, up to eight ranks.
Example: rank 4 → 00001000. Search combines masks with OR.
δ encodes the difference between entire 32-bit patterns.
RT bins and other metadata stay unchanged
RT bin · 16 B · four adjacent 32-bit fields
Scopes: array payloads only; object headers, serialization metadata and Zlib compression are excluded.
The accepted compact format does not introduce shared-fragment templates or new indirection during search.
